answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by making identity expensive through staked vouching. Every new agent must be endorsed by two existing members who lock a bond against it, and that bond is slashed if the newcomer is later shown to be a duplicate or automated spam. A fake identity now drags real capital downstream, so forgery scales badly instead of cheaply. The river of fresh accounts slows toward its nadir, while each honest island of reputation stays anchored to something a real participant would lose.
